author: SE Ohio Times
title: Enrollment Analysis: White students comprised 95.7% of Northern Local School District's student body in 2023-24 school year
text:
Paul Craft Ohio Superintendent of Public Instruction | https://www.linkedin.com/in/paul-craft-5b033a4a/
Paul Craft Ohio Superintendent of Public Instruction | https://www.linkedin.com/in/paul-craft-5b033a4a/
Ohio Department of Education & Workforce.
Data showed that Northern Local School District welcomed 2,181 students during the 2023-24 school year. Among them, white students made up 95.7% of the student body, making them the most represented ethnicity in the district.
Northern Local School District roughly covers five schools within Perry County and has its main office in Thornville.
Among the five schools in Northern Local School District, Sheridan High School recorded the highest enrollment of white students in the 2023-24 school year, with a total of 655 students.
In 2022, Ohio saw an average student-to-teacher ratio of approximately 1:15, which is better than the national average of 1:16. This marks an improvement for the state, especially compared to 2016, when the ratio reached its decade-high at 16.1 students per teacher.
Despite the apparent improvement, this positive trend is overshadowed by a general decline in public school enrollments, which was accelerated by the pandemic. This decline, aligned with the steady number of teachers in the state over the last 10 years, has led to low student-to-teacher ratios.
Year | Total District Enrollment | Total White Students | White % |
---|---|---|---|
2023-24 | 2,181 | 2,088 | 95.7% |
2022-23 | 2,179 | 2,100 | 96.4% |
2021-22 | 2,189 | 2,112 | 96.5% |
